Subject: AcquiRex: post-demo latency/throughput follow-up & SLA-driven tests

Laura —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Appreciated the candidness on expected load patterns and the QPS profiles your infra team shared. A quick recap so we have aligned next steps and to unblock the competitive tests you asked about: 

1) What we observed (from your side): you mentioned AcquiRex internal tests showed p95 ~240ms and p99 ~420ms against Hyperscale’s managed endpoint for short prompts (<=128 tokens) but saw big divergence at longer contexts (>1k tokens).
2) What Redwood saw during the demo: our staging run (same sample set) produced p95 ~170ms and p99 ~320ms for the short prompt set, and we saw better steady-state token/s when using continuous batching + KV cache on our Dedicated profile.

Proposed A/B test matrix (to confirm):
- Short prompt (<=128 tokens), steady QPS burst -> measure p95/p99 and tokens/sec
- Long context (1k–4k tokens), streaming enabled -> measure tail latency and prefix-cache hit rates
- Sustained throughput (48–72 hour soak) with 4x and 8x GPUs -> report tokens/sec and any degradation of p95/p99 over time

Can you:
- Share the sample payloads you used in Hyperscale tests (we can mirror them exactly) — attached is our example payload file (acquirex-sample-payloads.json).
- Confirm whether the Hyperscale numbers you quoted are from single-region runs or multi-region?
- Provide a small set of perf logs (headers + timing only) for 20 representative requests if available. Ops contact copied on this email.

We attached the demo recording and a quick CSV with our short-run p95/p99 snapshots. We'll draft a concrete test plan and SLA targets once we confirm the inputs. Suggested acceptance criteria proposal we think is defensible for contract language: p95 <= 180ms for short prompts, p99 <= 350ms, and sustained tokens/sec >= 10k on an 8-GPU pool (subject to payload mix). Happy to adjust with your ops team.

Next steps: if AcquiRex can share sample payloads and a short availability window for the lab run, we’ll provision an isolated Dedicated pool and schedule the A/B runs.

Thanks —
Priyom

Adding the technical checklist and a proposed runbook so the lab team and AcquiRex ops have a single source of truth.

Quick runbook (high level):
- Environment: isolated Redwood Dedicated pool (8x A100-equivalent GPUs) in us-west; identical config for Hyperscale mirror where possible.
- Models: Redwood-verified open model v2.3 (FP16), and a quantized int8 variant for the same architecture. We will run both for A/B.
- Keys to measure: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec (avg & 95th), KV cache hit ratio, GPU util, host-side queue depth, network e2e (client->gateway->worker).
- Test cases:
  * Case A: short prompts (<=128 tokens), bursty 300 RPS window for 10 minutes -> 5 iterations
  * Case B: long contexts (1k–4k tokens) streaming, progressive context growth -> single 60-minute window
  * Case C: soak test: 48-hour continuous run at 25% peak QPS, then 72-hour at 60% peak QPS (observe tail regression)
- Logging: we will provide a secure S3 bucket with a structured CSV/NDJSON dump (timestamped). We request AcquiRex to provide the same format for Hyperscale runs so we can do apples-to-apples analysis.

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- Short prompt: p95 <= 180ms; p99 <= 350ms
- Long context: p95 relative delta vs Hyperscale <= 10% (to account for different batching strategies)
- Soak: sustained tokens/sec drop <= 15% over 72 hours

Operational asks for AcquiRex ops:
- Provide the 20 representative log lines Priyom requested (headers + timings); prefer NDJSON if possible.
- Confirm whether there are any strict egress/cost limits during the Dedicated run (we can throttle).

I'll prepare the ephemeral infra and a test harness script (runbook + data collectors) and post links to the shared workspace.

Marissa Cole

Thanks all for the alignment. TL;DR: we run the A/B + soak during Nov 28–30 initial window, Redwood to own provisioning and run orchestration; AcquiRex to supply sample payloads and the 20 log extracts by Nov 24.

Concrete assignments:
- Redwood (Marissa + infra): provision 8x pool, deploy runbook, provide S3 bucket + monitoring hooks (Prometheus endpoints, GPU util, queue depth) by Nov 26.
- AcquiRex (Laura + ops): provide sample payloads (done), 20 sample log lines NDJSON by Nov 24, confirm egress/cost guardrails.
- Redwood sales (Priyom): Draft an SLA paragraph for proposal that reflects the acceptance criteria in Marissa's email and include a fallback policy (graceful degradation to lower-cost model variant). Priyom to circulate draft by Nov 20.

Acceptance criteria (finalize for contract):
- Short prompt p95 <= 180ms and p99 <= 350ms (us-west, single-region)
- Sustained tokens/sec >= 10k on 8-GPU pool with <=15% degradation over 72h soak
- If p95 target misses by >20% for two consecutive runs, automatic rollback to fallback model and remediation plan within 24 hours

If that timeline works, I’ll mark the deal stage in CRM and route a draft SOW to legal once Priyom posts the SLA paragraph.
